Guideline2: Avoid walking or driving through flood water.
Guideline3: Switch off electricity and gas supply.
Guideline4: Carry emergency kit and drinking water.

Guideline2: Do not use matches, candles, or open flames immediately after an earthquake.
Guideline3: Repair structural cracks in buildings before reoccupying them.
Guideline4: Secure overhead lights and heavy objects to reduce injury risk.
Guideline5: Follow BIS earthquake-resistant building standards for construction and repairs.

Guideline1: Move away from landslide-prone slopes and valleys immediately.
Guideline2: Stay alert for warning signs like ground cracks, falling rocks, or unusual sounds.
Guideline3: Follow evacuation orders and move to designated safe shelters.
Guideline4: Avoid constructing or staying near unstable slopes and drainage paths.
Guideline5: Do not touch fallen electrical wires and assist injured people only if it is safe to do so.

Guideline1: Monitor official weather warnings and avoid spreading rumours.
Guideline2: Evacuate immediately to designated shelters when instructed by authorities.
Guideline3: Stay indoors, secure doors and windows, and switch off the main electricity supply.
Guideline4: Keep an emergency kit with food, drinking water, medicines, flashlight, and batteries ready.
Guideline5: Do not go outside until officials confirm that the cyclone has completely passed.

Guideline1: Report any unattended or out-of-control fire to the local fire service or forest authorities immediately.
Guideline2: Never leave a campfire or open fire unattended; extinguish it completely before leaving.
Guideline3: Do not throw cigarettes, matchsticks, or other burning materials in forest areas.
Guideline4: Avoid burning crop residue, dry waste, or garbage near forests.
Guideline5: Keep emergency supplies ready and know the nearest evacuation route.

Guideline1: Drink plenty of water and stay hydrated even if you are not thirsty.
Guideline2: Follow weather updates through official news, radio, TV, or weather apps.
Guideline3: Wear light-coloured, loose cotton clothing and cover your head when outdoors.
Guideline4: Drink ORS, lemon water, buttermilk, coconut water, or other fluids to prevent dehydration.
Guideline5: Take extra care of children, elderly people, and those with health conditions during extreme heat.

Guideline1: Seek shelter immediately if you notice dark clouds, thunder, or signs of lightning.
Guideline2: Follow the 30-30 rule: if thunder follows lightning within 30 seconds, move indoors and stay there for at least 30 minutes after the last thunder.
Guideline3: Keep electrical earthing properly maintained to protect electrical equipment.
Guideline4: Trim trees that may fall on buildings during storms.
Guideline5: Stay indoors and avoid open areas until the storm has completely passed.

Guideline1: Check weather and avalanche forecasts before travelling to snow-covered mountains.
Guideline2: Move sideways to escape the avalanche path whenever possible.
Guideline3: Try to stay near the snow surface using a swimming motion if caught in an avalanche.
Guideline4: Cover your nose and mouth or create an air pocket in front of your face to improve breathing.
Guideline5: After the avalanche stops, dig yourself out if possible and mark the location of trapped people for rescuers.
